title: The gate ladder: affected checks per task, the full gate and tree scanners per phase, CI under eight minutes
description: The same full set of checks runs per task, per phase, locally and in CI several times, and the set is large because the product carries its own tree lints as tests. Measured: a task gate in the dogfood plan took 716 s, of which the sweep was 384 s and the panel browser gate 282 s; a narrow task gate measured 1,327 s because derived affected steps re-ran 506 s of suites its own full-sweep key had already run; the sweep is 6 min 36 s of wall and 34.6 min of CPU, and CI runs take 12 to 15 minutes. The CI half of this ladder (one executable gate description, skip of a green SHA, the codec cells) is already the earlier F1 phase's; this phase adds the per-task and per-phase rungs and the remaining speed.
desiredOutcome: A task's gate is the selection of checks its change affects, trusted only after its miss rate was measured on this repository's history; tree scanners and the full gate, browser steps included, run once per phase and on push, never per task; a probe of the guarded lints runs at sign-off only when the phase changed them; the sweep's wall clock is under four minutes and CI is under eight minutes and 55 runner-minutes, each measured with the same command before and after; one commit verb writes the index and the shard together, so adding a task mid-phase never leaves the plan uncommittable; and red-first through a sweep-shaped command proves when the task's suites pass.

findings.issue: contradicts task clause: acceptance (5) 'the measured result over 20 commits is recorded in the task outcome with the commit range'. The outcome records a 2-commit window (ad586f07b..d33730d60) in which one commit timed out at 1200s (NOT MEASURED) and the other was a full-set selection ('so no suite can be missed'), giving 'misses 0 of 1 commits (mutation); 0 of 1 runs (CI)'. That is zero evidence about the miss rate and not the 20-commit measurement the clause asks for; the executor itself says the 20-commit run is 'still owed by the orchestrator'. The 'misses 0 of 1' line must not be read as a clean miss rate.
findings.resolution: Run the 20-commit command the outcome names on a quiet machine (python3 tools/measure-affected-miss.py --commits 20 --budget-minutes 240 --timeout 2400 --ci-limit 30 --json) and record its output and commit range in the outcome before the task closes done; or, if the orchestrator decides the measurement is out of scope for this task, split it into its own task rather than close this one as met. If the task is closed with no change (--no-change --reason), the reason must say acceptance (5) is unmeasured.

findings.issue: P142.3's description is a verbatim re-ask of a task already done (b52ba79a, amended 66b3635d): tools/measure-affected-miss.py has existed since P131.16-dau, so this task adds nothing and its tests.add entries are met only by pre-existing cases m6, m8, m10, m13. A duplicate task in the plan is an input error that wastes an executor run and can double-count 'tests added'.
findings.resolution: Close P142.3 with --no-change and a reason naming b52ba79a/66b3635d and the pre-existing cases, after (5) is measured; or rewrite its description to the measurement alone.

findings.issue: contradicts task clause "a phase touching no such file runs none and says so" / acceptance (2) "prints that it ran none" on the held path: a run that printed `ran none` is held as `state["lintProbe"] = {"head": head}` (the word is not stored), and the held branch then appends `lint probe green (held at this HEAD)` - so any re-entry at the same HEAD (e.g. after the sign-off verb stopped) reports a probe that ran no row as green, the exact reading-as-a-proof the clause forbids.
findings.resolution: Store the word with the hold (`{"head": head, "said": "ran none"|"green"}`) and echo it on the held branch (`lint probe ran none (held at this HEAD)`); add an lp6 twin that holds a ran-none run and asserts the held did-line says ran none.

findings.issue: The success print breaks the module's stated invariant `INSTRUCTION_BYTES = 300` ("The bound every print that is not a stop stays inside") whenever a probe runs: the executor's own measurement is 312 bytes in lp1's one-task fixture. This repo keeps tools/prove-gates.py, so from this change every sign-off here prints past the bound; lp1 does not assert the bound and dp3 only measures a probeless fixture, so nothing goes red.
findings.resolution: Make the probe clause fit (e.g. fold it into the `invariants clean` clause as `invariants clean, lint probe green|ran none`, or move the word into the sign-off summary) and extend dp3 (or lp1/lp2) to measure the success print of a probe-carrying fixture against INSTRUCTION_BYTES.

findings.issue: A shipped product script now executes any project file that happens to sit at `tools/prove-gates.py` at every sign-off, by filename convention alone, with no plan key opting in: a user project with an unrelated script at that path has it run with `--changed <paths>` and its exit 1 read as a not-proven stop and any other non-zero exit as a refusal that blocks sign-off. Every other gate the driver runs is named by the plan (meta.buildCommands, meta.runtimeBoot); this one is not. The executor flagged it as (b).
findings.resolution: Key the probe off the plan (a `meta.buildCommands` entry or a dedicated meta key naming the probe command and declaring it speaks the `--changed` protocol), absent means skip; set it in this repo's plan. If that is out of this task's files, file it as a fix task before sign-off rather than shipping the filename convention.

findings.issue: Acceptance (4) is checked as equality of porcelain status letters + paths only. A file already dirty before the run (` M`) that the probe leaves mutated still reads ` M` after, so a stranded mutation in an already-modified lint file passes; conversely, a second session editing the shared checkout during the minutes-long run produces a false `left the checkout changed` stop whose remedy (`restore the tree`) would tell the operator to discard someone else's work.
findings.resolution: For entries dirty before the run, also compare a content digest (git hash-object of each) before and after; and word the stop as 'changed during the probe run' naming the entries without prescribing a restore, or refuse to start the probe when a path in the changed set is already dirty.

findings.issue: `subprocess.run` of a minutes-long mutating probe carries no timeout, so a hung probe hangs the sign-off step indefinitely with the tree possibly mid-mutation.
findings.resolution: Pass a timeout (a generous bound or one read from the plan), catch `subprocess.TimeoutExpired` as a refusal stop; the status comparison in `finally` already reports what a killed run left.

findings.issue: lp6's 'at another HEAD it runs once' twin calls `lint_probe(..., None)`, which short-circuits the hold on `if head and ...`; it never exercises a different SHA, so a hold that ignored the head comparison (e.g. `held.get("head")` truthy) would still pass lp6.
findings.resolution: Call the twin with a different 40-hex head (`"b" * 40`) so the comparison itself is what lets it run.

findings.issue: contradicts task clause 'Split each into staged blocks so the sweep spreads them across workers, and re-record the cost table.' The table is untouched, so the four split files keep the figures they had when each ran unsplit on one slot. Those figures now set the shard balance and every split file's timeout. On the live table, shard 3/3 holds three staged suites in a row (test_close_phase 330.3, test__deps 268.2, test_stamp_verification 265.4). The per-block process overhead on Windows, where test_stamp_verification now starts a process for each of its blocks, has never been measured. The executor gives a reason (the table binds to windows-latest and cannot be recorded from darwin), but the clause is still not done.
findings.resolution: Make it a tracked task before sign-off. Once this lands on a CI run, save each Windows selftests cell's log and run `python tools/sweep-selftests.py --costs-from-log <logs> --platform windows-latest --record-costs .github/sweep-costs.json`. findings.issue: The diff makes three untouched documents state the old admission rule. CLAUDE.md says a staged suite 'is admitted with `stage_grant(jobs)` slots', CONTRIBUTING.md says 'is admitted holding `stage_grant(jobs)` slots', and the ci.yml comment says 'a staged suite is admitted holding all but one of them'. After slot_gate's change at tools/sweep-selftests.py:1385-1394, a suite holds as many slots as are free when its turn comes, between 1 and that number. The executor listed all three as stale and outside its files.
findings.resolution: Reword each to say: up to `stage_grant(jobs)` slots, as many as are free when its turn comes and at least one, with the number it holds passed to the child in SWEEP_STAGE_GRANT and its timeout calibrated to that number.

findings.issue: A staged suite's grant is fixed when it is admitted. If it is admitted with 1 slot, it runs every block serially (stage_workers=min(6,1)) for its whole run, even after other slots free up. Its timeout at held=1 is 3 x cost, which can exceed SWEEP_DEADLINE. tt5 still only bounds timeouts at the full grant, and its label was widened to accept that the deadline 'cuts ... a staged suite admitted late with fewer slots'. On today's windows table this is latent, not live. At jobs=4 the staged suite second in each shard gets 1 slot (shard 2/3: test_commit_task_work 222.9; shard 3/3: test__deps 268.2), and both serial costs are well under the 1380 s deadline. A rebalance that put test_audit_task (606.0) or test_drive_phase (1346.4) second in a shard would have the deadline cut a run that is slow, not hung, and nothing would turn red first.
findings.resolution: Add a tt5 sibling over the live table: for each `--shard i/3` at jobs=4, compute each staged suite's admitted slots (ticket order, with what is free at its turn, assuming earlier holders have not yet finished). Assert that file_timeout at those slots, and the serial cost it implies, stay under SWEEP_DEADLINE. That makes the latent case fail on the table change that creates it.

findings.file: tools/sweep-selftests.py:1761-1765 (one_block's timeout); cases tools/sweep-selftests.py:4007 bg6, :4306 tt0, :4321 tt1

findings.file: CLAUDE.md:239-243; CONTRIBUTING.md:330-334; .github/workflows/ci.yml:134-135; tools/sweep-selftests.py:1713 (sweep docstring), :1587-1590 (costs_from_rows docstring), :1604-1612 (record_costs 'about' text), :1474-1478 (shard comment)
findings.issue: These still describe the grant model the diff retired for every staged suite in the tree. CLAUDE.md says a staged_main suite 'is admitted with stage_grant(jobs) slots ... and is told the number in SWEEP_STAGE_GRANT, which sizes its block pool'. CONTRIBUTING.md and the ci.yml comment say the same. sweep()'s docstring says '`costs` orders the submissions (`run_order`)', but sweep() now orders by work_items. costs_from_rows, the shard comment and the record_costs 'about' string say the recorded figure is 'wall seconds times the slots ... the file held', but a block-run suite's figure is now the sum of its processes' seconds. The 'about' string is written into the committed .github/sweep-costs.json on the next --record-costs. The executor named the first three as followers, but no case and no task holds them.
findings.resolution: Rewrite each to the block model in this task or a follower task filed before sign-off: blocks are run as the sweep's jobs, one slot each, and replayed via --replay; a suite whose STAGES is not a literal runs whole on a grant; a block-run suite's cost is the summed slot-seconds of its processes. Fix sweep()'s docstring to name work_items.

findings.issue: sh6 says 'a shard runs its costliest files FIRST, so the slowest suite starts at once', but it asserts run_order(), which sweep() no longer calls. Submission order is now work_items (:1743). bb3 pins work_items as a function, but no case shows that sweep() submits in that order. Reverting :1743 to any other order leaves sh6 and bb3 green. bb1 uses equal costs, so it cannot tell either.
findings.resolution: Retitle sh6 to what it asserts: the split's order. Add a case that sweeps, at jobs=1, a heavy plain file and a staged fixture whose per-block estimate is higher, with costs given, and reads the order off each row's windows (start times): costliest job first.

findings.issue: replayed() keeps the first entry for a label (by.setdefault) and drops any later one silently. A list naming one block twice - the shape a sweep that ran a block twice would hand over - replays one copy and is never named. The sweep cannot produce that today: labels are unique by stage_labels, paths are set-deduped, and there is one counter per suite. But the replay is meant to be the honest reading, and it names a missing block and a stray block yet not a doubled one.
findings.resolution: Count labels in entries. A label listed more than once becomes one failing case '<label> RAN TWICE'. Add it to sr15's list, red-first by restoring setdefault.

findings.issue: The clause 'at some moment blocks of both run' rests on a-blocks sleeping 0.3 s, measured inside each child after its own interpreter start. It fails whenever b1's sleep starts more than 0.3 s after the last a-block's sleep began. That is start-up jitter, which the executor itself measured at load average 18-20 on 10 cores, and this case runs inside a full sweep's 8 workers. The other clauses (two b blocks at once, never more than four) are robust.
findings.resolution: Lengthen the a nap (for example 1.5 s, still well under b's 3 s), or read concurrency off the rows' per-process windows that sweep() now returns, rather than off in-sleep spans.

1. A holder whose work lives in its own task tree (its marker/provenance via _worktrees, the same reading the drive uses) cannot be holding the project checkout's change - do not charge it.
2. A change whose bytes match the starting task's own most recent filed return stamp (the scope/dirty digests stamp-verification computes - reuse that function, do not reimplement a digest) is that task's own work: not a refusal.
3. The refusal never names a command any guard in this plugin refuses; drop the stash remedy and name the supported ones (finish/unblock the holder, or commit it).

Keep the refusal for the case it exists for (another checkout-resident task's genuinely unfinished work). Red-first each case; prove the remaining refusal still fires. High risk: this guards against one task's commit sweeping in another's work. No F/P/BUG ids in comments.
